content: This medication, commonly known by the brand name Viberzi, is used to treat a specific gastrointestinal condition called irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D). It works by slowing down the movement of the gut to alleviate symptoms. Before starting this medication, read the Medication Guide provided by your pharmacist, and review it again each time you get a refill. Take this medication orally with food, as directed by your doctor, typically twice daily. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and any other medications you may be taking. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements. Do not increase your dose, use this medication more frequently, or take it for longer than prescribed. Doing so will not improve your condition faster and may increase the risk of side effects. To achieve the best results, use this medication consistently as directed. If you are also taking loperamide to manage diarrhea, avoid using it on a regular schedule, as it may lead to constipation. However, it can be used occasionally for severe diarrhea if needed. While this medication is effective for many individuals, it may sometimes lead to addiction. The risk of addiction is higher if you have a history of substance use disorder, such as overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol. To minimize this risk, take the medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Common side effects of this medication include constipation, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or drowsiness. If any of these effects persist or worsen, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. If you experience any unusual symptoms, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking eluxadoline, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause drowsiness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can increase this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages, and discuss marijuana use with your doctor. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether eluxadoline passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Do not share this medication with others. Laboratory tests, such as liver function tests and lipase levels, may be conducted while you are taking this medication to monitor your condition. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in a secure location to prevent theft, misuse, or abuse. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
